posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

Where did the antimatter go? The Big Bang should have created equal amounts of matter and antimatter, which would have annihilated each other instantly. So why does anything exist at all? Scientists are still hunting for the missing half of reality.

But thanks to new techniques for DNA sequencing, dating ancient detritus, mathematical models, and aerial and lidar archaeology, we are now able to get a faint idea of what this world might have looked and felt like.

This bearded reedling was photographed in Landvik, Norway, and it might have the most stylish mustache in the bird world.⁠
⁠
Only the males have those black markings, and they’re more than just for looks. Males with longer “mustaches” usually win when competing for food, and females tend to prefer them too.⁠
⁠

Ever heard of a limpia? 🌿🥚 It’s a traditional cleansing ritual you can experience at local markets in Cuenca, Ecuador!⁠
For just $3.50, you can sit down with a practitioner and experience this fascinating ceremony. It begins with bundles of herbs being brushed and tapped over your body, followed by an egg being passed over you to symbolically draw out negative energy. ⁠
⁠

The way deer interact with people at Nara Park when food is involved is honestly the cutest thing ever. 🦌😂⁠
They bow for a treat, patiently wait for more, and sometimes get a little too enthusiastic about asking for snacks. ⁠
⁠
These adorable little interactions make visiting Nara Park in Japan such a unique experience! ⁠
🎥: @steparria

A boxing match where the fighters sit on a bamboo pole? 🥊🎋 Only in Thailand!⁠
At the Karen Local Market near Chiang Mai, this playful traditional-style contest brings two opponents face-to-face as they balance on a bamboo stick and try to knock each other off. ⁠
⁠
It looks like a whole lot of fun, but staying balanced is clearly part of the challenge! 😂⁠

Harvest mice are the smallest rodents in Europe, weighing just 5–11 grams, about as much as a small coin. Their tail works like an extra hand, gripping stems as they climb and balance with ease. ⁠
⁠
And when it’s time to rest, they curl up in round nests they weave from grass, each one about the size of a tennis ball.

The Atlantic crossing ceremony… 😂🌊 First, they put you through the whole initiation, then they literally wash it all off you!⁠
⁠
It’s part of the maritime tradition known as “Crossing the Line,” traditionally held when a ship crosses the Equator. First-timers, nicknamed “pollywogs,” face a series of funny, messy challenges before being welcomed into the ancient seafarers’ club as “shellbacks.”⁠

Hotel Arbez, in the village of La Cure, sits directly on the border between France and Switzerland, and the line runs right through the dining room, the kitchen, and even the bed in the honeymoon suite.⁠
⁠
Its location has shaped its history in surprising ways. ⁠
⁠
During World War II, because the lower staircase was in France and the upper floor belonged to neutral Switzerland, German occupying forces could only enter the French portion.⁠
⁠

Vienna’s Christmas market has a little magic in the sky. ❤️✨⁠
At Rathausplatz, the famous Herzerlflug sees a giant glowing heart fly over the Heart Tree every 30 minutes after dark, a beautiful sight that makes the festive atmosphere even more special.⁠
⁠
Definitely one to add to your Christmas market bucket list!⁠
🎥: @tripswithisa

@j.looten captured this “Desert Staircase” in Chile’s Atacama Desert, near San Pedro de Atacama, a stone structure that lets visitors look out over a nearby geoglyph.⁠
⁠
To make the stairs flow into the Milky Way, he shot a nearly 360° panorama and projected it vertically. ⁠
⁠
On the horizon, you can spot the Licancabur volcano, rising 5,916 m on the border between Chile and Bolivia.
